description: Inputs to tools/world/reality/extent.py. The extent is derived from data with these rules; the numbers here are the only hand-chosen values and each one carries its reason. Output: config/extent.json + library layer 'extent_zone'.

acquisition_bbox_lonlat.reason: Search window for raw acquisition, deliberately wider than any plausible extent so the extent rules (not the download box) decide what is kept.

core.reason: Core = every coastline-derived land polygon touching the Key West city-limit polygon (Overture divisions, from OSM/Census) plus Stock Island, the island between Key West and the bridge.

context_landmasses.reason: Author rule: Boca Chica is not a playable district. Only its outline on the bridge side, terrain and coastline are kept; its buildings, roads, vegetation and infrastructure are not ingested (counted in the report).

adjacent_islands.reason: Islets are adjacent when their nearest land is the core (not Boca Chica) and they lie within the search radius. The resulting gaps show a natural break (all core-side islets are <= ~0.5 km; the next land is Boca-Chica-side), reported in extent.json.

crossings.reason: The severed US-1 crossing is kept whole as reality; the far landing plus one water-margin of Boca Chica outline gives the in-world end of the broken bridge.

water_margin_reason: Two times the adjacency break (~0.5 km): every shoreline structure attached to included land lies inside, and the sea/ice continues past every coast instead of ending at the data edge.
never_cut_land_reason: Any non-context land polygon that crosses the rectangle grows the rectangle until it is fully inside (iterated). Context landmasses are the only land the boundary may cross.
contain_legacy_runtime_crop_reason: The new extent is a superset of the committed 2 m runtime crop, so nothing currently in the game falls outside the library.
